title: Stargazer ops digest — night shift summary and follow-ups (2028-11-11)
content:
Purpose: quick handoff for the night-to-day transition. This is an operational snapshot — incidents, mitigations we applied, and concrete follow-ups for the next rotation. Keep the latest runbook bits (see linked PR + Confluence) during morning call.

SUMMARY (top lines)
- Time window: 2028-11-11 22:05 — 2028-11-12 02:40 UTC. Primary symptom was intermittent 95th/99th tail latency spikes for hosted generation endpoints (models > 8k context) starting ~22:10 UTC.
- Root cause (initial): cascade of KV cache invalidations triggered by a noisy periodic job (metrics-backfill job) + autoscaler policy mis-evaluating CPU headroom on dedicated pools, which led to a number of cold model driver restarts and elevated token generation latency.
- Impact: ~4% of requests experienced 95p latency > 1200ms, several customer routes briefly breached latency SLOs. No data exfiltration. Alerts: LatencyAlert-P95 and PoolHealth-HighRestart.
- Current status: mitigated; baseline restored by 02:40 UTC. Post-incident actions in progress.

TIMELINE (concise)
- 22:05 UTC: Pager hit — LatencyAlert-P95 for hosted/generation:v2. Alert page -> #sre-ops.
- 22:08 UTC: Quick triage: spike pattern correlated with high error/retry backoff logs and a surge of cache-miss rates in /kv-cache/hits.
- 22:15 UTC: Identified correlating cron job in infra (metrics-backfill-runner) running heavy scan of redis keys every 5m due to a config drift. Spike aligns with run time.
- 22:30 UTC: Autoscaler for dedicated pool A evaluated resource signals incorrectly (bug in the weight calculation introduced in PR 888) -> triggered scale-in/scale-out thrash for driver pods.
- 23:05 UTC: Applied immediate mitigations: paused metrics-backfill job (infra), bumped dedicated pool min-replicas to preserve warm workers (sre oncall), and reverted autoscaler weight change to previous safe commit (PR 905 revert).
- 23:40 UTC: Observe p95 fell to ~450ms but still above normal. Decided to run warmers to repopulate KV cache prefixes for hot routes.
- 00:30 UTC: Warmers completed first pass for top-10 routes. p95 back to normal (~200-250ms).
- 02:40 UTC: Confirmed system stable for 45+ minutes and closed pager.

WHAT WE DID (commands / quick refs)
- Paused job: kubectl -n infra scale job/metrics-backfill-runner --replicas=0 (see infra/playbooks/cron-control).
- Bumped pool min: rwi pool update dedicated-A --min 6 -> was 3.
- Revert autoscaler change: git revert 3a9f8d2 (PR 905 revert) + rolling restart of scaler controller.
- Warmers: internal tool run: ./tools/cache-warmer --routes top10 --parallel 8 --model-gen --dry-run=false (logs in s3://redwood-ops/warmers/2028-11-11-night/).
- Log queries: production Kibana saved search "kv-cache-miss-spike-2028-11-11"; Grafana dashboard: /d/serving/latency-by-context.

NOTABLE OBSERVATIONS
- Cache miss rate for KV namespace model-attention increased by ~78x during initial spike window. The keyspace had larger-than-expected churn due to the metrics job scanning keys and TTL rewrites.
- Autoscaler weight formula change (PR 888) had a subtle effect when combined with short-lived restart cycles; once scale-in occurred, new pods started cold and boosted latency while requests backed up.
- A single customer route (customer-phi-chat) accounted for ~46% of the hot keys touched by the metrics job because of high internal testing load — flagged to account team.

TO-DO / FOLLOW-UPS (owners + ETA)
1) Infra: Add guardrail to metrics-backfill-runner to limit keys-per-run and use scan cursor properly. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2028-11-16. Artifact: PR link in linked_artifacts when ready.
2) Serving Runtime: Rework autoscaler weight fallback to handle transient restarts without aggressive scale-in. Owner: Ethan Park. ETA: 2028-11-14. Related PR: TODO (start branch "autoscaler-fallback").
3) SRE runbook: Edit "Cache Warmers Runbook" to include: pre-flight check for metrics job, emergency pause steps, and explicit warmer invocation examples with expected run time. Owner: Maya Chen (me). ETA: 2028-11-13. Confluence page above.
4) Customer success: Reach out to account for customer-phi-chat to coordinate reduced noisy testing during peak hours. Owner: Liam O'Connor (CS liaison). ETA: 2028-11-12 (morning).
5) Observability: Add an anomaly alert for KV namespace churn (new Grafana alert). Owner: Observability team (tagging @obs-team). ETA: 2028-11-18.

RUNBOOK PATCH NOTES (quick diffs for the morning)
- Section: "cache-thermostat" -> add pre-check step: query: "SELECT count(*) FROM kv.events WHERE ttl_updated=true AND timestamp > now() - 10m" (example).
- Emergency pause snippet: kubectl patch job/metrics-backfill-runner --patch '{"spec": {"suspend": true}}' and fallback to manual cursor scanning.
- Add a short script to run warmers in parallel and stream progress to /ops/warmers/ (candidate script: tools/ops/run_warmers.sh).

BRIEF NOTES FOR NEXT SHIFT (what to run/look at in first 20 minutes)
- Confirm pool A min-replicas still at 6 and autoscaler revert is rolling (kubectl get deploy -n infra scaler-controller -o wide).
- Check Grafana panels: p95 latency (hosted/generation), pool restart rate, kv-cache miss ratio.
- Tail warmer logs: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-ops/warmers/2028-11-11-night/ ; grep for errors.
- Verify metrics-backfill is still suspended in CronJobs (kubectl -n infra get cronjob metrics-backfill-runner).
- Re-run saved Kibana query for error traces: "generation-coldstart-traces" and triage anything > 3 occurrences in last hour.

DECISIONS / RISK ACCEPTANCES MADE DURING SHIFT
- Elevated min-replicas temporarily to avoid cascading cold starts at cost of some extra GPU hours (accepted by oncall).
- Paused a non-critical infra job (metrics-backfill) — acceptable short-term risk; we will restore under throttling rules.

INCIDENTS / PAGERS (short list)
- LatencyAlert-P95 (hosted/generation:v2) — raised 22:05 UTC; resolved 02:40 UTC. Pager severity: Sev3. Link: SRE-4821.
- PoolHealth-HighRestart (dedicated-A) — multiple restarts 22:20-23:00 UTC. Mitigated by bumping min replicas + revert.

LESSONS & SUGGESTIONS (postmortem kernels)
- Avoid running broad keyspace scans from periodic infra jobs without strict rate-limiting and clear TTL respect.
- Autoscaler changes need a staged rollout: A/B test on a small pool, include a transient-restart detection.
- Invest in faster programmatic warmers triggered as a part of scaling events (autoscaler -> warmer hook).

MISC/NOTES TO SELF
- I saved a trimmed JSON of the warmers output to s3 and uploaded basic metrics to the incident ticket.
- PR 905 revert link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/905 (apply follow-up test).

CONTACTS / ESCALATION PATHS
- Infra lead: Priya Nair (pager), Slack: @priya.nair.
- Serving runtime lead: Ethan Park, Slack: @ethanp.
- CS liaison: Liam O'Connor, Slack: @liam.

If anything flares in the morning, escalate to oncall+team leads and follow the postmortem template in Confluence.

---
Quick sign-off: Maya (night oncall).
